API Reference¶

Python library to create satellites and tasks and solve the scheduling problem with a genetic programming algorithm.

class scheduler.FitnessEvaluator¶

Bases: pybind11_object

Evaluates a population of GP individuals by simulating a greedy schedule with each individual’s expression tree as the priority function.

After evaluation every Individual in the population will have its fitness field set to a scalar value that reflects how well the tree minimised response time and energy consumption.

Fitness formula¶

Three raw objectives are collected for each individual:

  • compRatio – fraction of available jobs that were successfully scheduled (higher is better).

  • meanResp – average response time (completion - arrival) in minutes (lower is better).

  • energy – total energy consumed across all satellites in watt- minutes (lower is better).

Each objective is normalised to [0, 1] across the current population so that differences in scale cannot dominate the result. The final fitness is then:

\[\begin{split}f = w_{\\text{jobs}} \\cdot \\widehat{r} - w_{\\text{time}} \\cdot \\widehat{t} - w_{\\text{energy}} \\cdot \\widehat{e}\end{split}\]

where \(\\hat{\\cdot}\) denotes population-normalised values and the default weights are (0.60, 0.25, 0.15).

Example

from scheduler import SchedulerGP, FitnessEvaluator, SimulationSnapshot
from scheduler import buildTerminalRegistry

gp   = SchedulerGP(satellites, jobs)
gp.initialize(populationSize=100)

eval = FitnessEvaluator(buildTerminalRegistry())

for generation in range(50):
    snap = SimulationSnapshot(current_minute, satellites, jobs)
    eval.evaluate(gp.getPopulation(), snap)  # writes fitness in place
    gp.solveNextGeneration()
evaluate(self: scheduler.FitnessEvaluator, population: scheduler.Population, snap: scheduler.SimulationSnapshot) → None¶

Score every individual in population and write the result into each individual’s fitness field.

This is the only method the main GP loop needs to call each generation.

Parameters:

  • population (list[Individual]) – The current GP population, obtained via SchedulerGP.getPopulation(). Each individual’s fitness field is updated in place.

  • snap (SimulationSnapshot) – Read-only snapshot of the current simulation state. The evaluator runs a fresh greedy simulation for every individual, so snap is never modified.

Notes

Fitness values are population-relative: the same tree may receive a different score in a different generation if the rest of the population has changed.

evaluate_single(self: scheduler.FitnessEvaluator, individual: scheduler.Individual, snap: scheduler.SimulationSnapshot) → tuple¶

Evaluate a single individual and return its raw (un-normalised) objectives.

Useful for inspecting the best individual after evolution has finished.

Parameters:

  • individual (Individual) – The GP individual to evaluate.

  • snap (SimulationSnapshot) – Simulation snapshot used for the evaluation.

Returns:

(comp_ratio, mean_response_time, total_energy)

  • comp_ratio – fraction of available jobs scheduled ∈ [0, 1].

  • mean_response_time – average (completion - arrival) in minutes.

  • total_energy – total energy consumed (watt-minutes).

Return type:

tuple[float, float, float]

property weightEnergy¶

Weight applied to the energy-consumption penalty. Default 0.15. Increase this to make the GP prefer energy-efficient satellite assignments.

property weightJobs¶

Weight applied to the completion-ratio reward term. Default 0.60. Increase this to make the GP prioritise scheduling as many jobs as possible.

property weightTime¶

Weight applied to the mean-response-time penalty. Default 0.25. Increase this to make the GP prioritise faster job turnaround.

class scheduler.SimulationSnapshot¶

Bases: pybind11_object

A self-contained, point-in-time snapshot of the simulation world.

The external application must construct and populate a snapshot before calling FitnessEvaluator.evaluate() for each GP generation. All satellite and job objects are copied into the snapshot, so subsequent changes to the originals have no effect on the evaluator.

Example

snap = scheduler.SimulationSnapshot(
    currentMinute = 0.0,
    satellites    = my_satellites,
    jobs          = my_jobs,
    uniformEnergy = 2.5,   # watts per minute per satellite
)
property currentMinute¶

Simulation clock at snapshot time (minutes from epoch).

property energyPerMinute¶

Energy consumed per minute of computation, indexed by satellite position in the satellites list. When non-empty this overrides uniformEnergy. Must have the same length as satellites if provided.

property jobs¶

Pool of jobs available for scheduling at this instant.

property satellites¶

Current state of every satellite in the constellation.

class scheduler.TerminalDef¶

Bases: pybind11_object

A named terminal variable used in GP expression trees (e.g. ‘job.priority’).

property name¶

Human-readable name of the terminal (e.g. 'job.priority').

scheduler.buildTerminalRegistry() → list[scheduler.TerminalDef]¶

Build and return the terminal registry used by the GP algorithm.

The registry maps human-readable names to field accessors that the expression tree evaluator uses to read job and satellite features at runtime. You must pass the returned list to FitnessEvaluator and, if you construct a TreeBuilder directly, to that as well.

Returns:

Ordered list of terminal definitions. The index of each entry corresponds to the terminalIndex stored in TERMINAL nodes of the expression tree.

Return type:

list[TerminalDef]

Example

from scheduler import buildTerminalRegistry, FitnessEvaluator

registry = buildTerminalRegistry()
evaluator = FitnessEvaluator(registry)
